Registers a host public key in the selected account known_hosts file and changes SSH authentication trust. The server may contact the supplied host to obtain its key; review the target and fingerprint before relying on it.
This mutation uses form POST. The source declares clean rollback; the client performs no automatic rollback or retry.

The host list and its nested host, key, line and metadata fields retain optional presence. Public keys, raw key bodies and fingerprints remain returned payload data; the client does not validate fingerprints or fetch further resources.

Omit port to retain the documented server default of 22; an explicitly supplied zero is sent unchanged and is not omission.

Checks the host public key against the selected account known_hosts file. Verification may contact the supplied SSH host; choosing a host is an explicit network action. This does not establish successful SSH authentication or server identity beyond the API result.

Payload status is an optional integer 0/1 flag: 1 means the host exists; 0 means it is absent or must be registered again. failure_type distinguishes new and changed hosts. Payload errors are distinct from UAPI envelope errors; UAPI status=0 remains a failure. Host records, fingerprints and status fields retain optional presence; no nullable fields are inferred.
